### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/view.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ae16687ad430f4f9870ea5ba2bc9b63d6f41fc31`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/view.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/view.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ae16687ad430f4f9870ea5ba2bc9b63d6f41fc31` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8f298a4addc1ff9ba464b4f30c91c23678ae519b` — the merge of head `2c75635eb43d820fc57b9fbc13b94cd3bbc3ec0f` into base `ae16687ad430f4f9870ea5ba2bc9b63d6f41fc31`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8f298a4addc1ff9ba464b4f30c91c23678ae519b && git checkout 8f298a4addc1ff9ba464b4f30c91c23678ae519b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ae16687ad430f4f9870ea5ba2bc9b63d6f41fc31 2c75635eb43d820fc57b9fbc13b94cd3bbc3ec0f && git checkout -B drift-repro ae16687ad430f4f9870ea5ba2bc9b63d6f41fc31 && git merge --no-ff 2c75635eb43d820fc57b9fbc13b94cd3bbc3ec0f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ae16687ad430f4f9870ea5ba2bc9b63d6f41fc31
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ae16687ad430f4f9870ea5ba2bc9b63d6f41fc31` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. Refusals and prescriptions — hold.** `FormViewSchema.type` is `enumWithRetiredValues(['simple','tabbed','wizard'], FORM_VIEW_TYPE_RETIRED).default('simple')` (`view.zod.ts` ≈L4614). The helper (`retired-key.ts:402`) returns a plain `ZodEnum` whose error map fires only on the retired member, so a misspelt value keeps zod's message and an omitted key materialises `simple` — the default is unchanged and `parse(parse(x))` is stable (a parsed form carries no retired member and no tombstoned key). The three prescriptions name live values only: `tabbed` / the `simple` default / `subforms` (declared on `FormViewSchema`), `navigation.mode` with `drawer` as the default (#26804 made `drawer` the default and retired `split`), the console's New/Edit dialogs sized by `modalSize`, and action `type: 'modal'` (`ActionType` enum, `action.zod.ts:585`). No prescription names `navigation.mode: 'split'`; the ruling's mapping is applied to the current tree exactly as the seat's claim ruling (1) directs, and the PR body says so. The split-only keys are `retiredKey()` tombstones: `FormSectionSchema.pane` (≈L4053, so the legacy `groups[]` alias is covered too — `groups` folds onto `sections` after the refinement, and the author's path is pinned in `view.test.ts`), `splitSize` and `splitResizable` (≈L4697–4699). The old `superRefine` that refused `pane` off a `split` form is removed; that is correct, since the tombstone now refuses the key on every layout at the section itself, and the remaining refinement (`features.*` root) still runs on both buckets. Doors: `FormViewSchema`, `ViewSchema.form` / `formViews.*`, `ViewItemSchema` form arms and the flattened `formOverlay` all build on `FormViewSchema` via `.extend` (≈L4177, L6698); `defineStack` → `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422; the `/meta` write door and Studio save parse `view` through `getMetadataTypeSchema('view')` = `ViewMetadataSchema` (`kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts:114`), whose arms are those same members. All five schema doors plus `defineStack` are pinned in the new test for each of the three values, and the three keys are pinned on each of the three layouts, in `sections` and in `groups`.

**2. ADR-0087 disposition — true in code and pinned.** D2 `form-view-presentation-types-removed` (`conversions/registry.ts`, MAJOR_18 order 78, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '18.2.0'`) deletes a retired `type` (the form lands on the `simple` default), strips `splitSize` / `splitResizable` and every `sections[].pane` / `groups[].pane`, over `mapViewPayloads` (a container's `form`, `formViews.*`, a form view item's `config`, the stored-row `{ views: [row] }` wrap) and the assembled `viewItems` channel. It is retired from the authoring funnel (`apply.ts:157` skips it unless `includeRetired`), and `applyConversionsToStoredItem` pins `includeRetired` to true (`stored.ts` header) — that primitive is what `packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts:884` calls per stored row, so a `sys_metadata` `view` row carrying `type: 'split' | 'drawer' | 'modal'`, `pane`, `splitSize` or `splitResizable` converts on read to a `simple` form, exactly as the changeset says. Pinned over a stored container (five notices, `ViewSchema.parse` of the output, copy-on-write), a stored form view item, idempotence, load-path absence, step-18 wiring and the D3 entry `ui-form-view-type-layout-only` (`conversionIds` names the D2; `acceptanceCriteria` present); the fixture's 9 notices are accounted for. Three `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` rows (`ui/FormSection:pane`, `ui/FormView:splitSize`, `ui/FormView:splitResizable`), a `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment (order 112, unique in the template) and a JOIN row in `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` (three value refusals + three tombstones). Stripping the keys on every form, not only `split` forms, is sound: `pane` off a `split` form was already a parse error on main, and `splitSize` / `splitResizable` were accepted on any `type` before, so a stored `tabbed` form carrying them now rehydrates clean. **Survey count:** I re-measured on `origin/main` with `git grep` — `pane:` authors are exactly `task.view.ts:424–425` and the lint fixture `:334–335`; retired `type` authorings in form-view shape are `task.view.ts:421` (`split`), `:431` (`drawer`), the lint fixture's copy, and the spec-typed `package-schema.ts:118` (`modal`); the two Studio enums (`anchors.ts:305`, `default-schemas.ts:223`); plus one docs comment the newest commit fixes (`content/docs/protocol/objectui/index.mdx:234`); no JSON fixture or seed. The PR's numbers match. The survey is repo-scoped by construction; live `sys_metadata` rows are not surveyable from here and the PR does not claim they are — the conversion above is the disposition for them, and that is the right answer to the question.

**3. The kept keys — true, and no sentence overclaims.** `react-blocks.ts:240–245`: the React `ObjectForm` block's `schema` is `FormViewSchema`, its `dataProps` include `drawerSide`, `drawerWidth`, `modalSize`, `splitDirection`, and its `formType` binding keeps `'split' | 'drawer' | 'modal'` (untouched here, #27159's). Live readers: `ObjectForm.tsx:559` (split arm → `SplitForm.tsx:474`), `:597–598` (drawer arm → `DrawerForm.tsx:304, 710–715`). The diff's claim that the three are **inert on a form view** is accurate in-repo: the only form-view routes into those arms are `RecordFormPage.tsx:324–339` (`pageFormType` is derived from `formDef.type`, so `'split'` is now unreachable; it still compiles because `['tabbed','wizard','split'].includes(formDef.type)` is a string-array read and the ternary's result narrows into the declared union) and `useActionModal.tsx:280` (`formType: 'modal'` → `ModalForm`, which reads `modalSize` only). No sentence in the diff says they are retired; `view.zod.ts` JSDoc and `liveness/view.json` both say "stays declared … leaves on #27159". `modalSize` "read on every layout" is true: `recordFormNavigation.ts:236–240` copies the form view's `modalSize` onto the record dialog irrespective of `type`. The liveness rows: `splitSize` / `splitResizable` → `dead` with REMOVED notes, `type` NARROWED, kept keys `live` with reasons; counts `76 / 7 / 83` consistent (two rows moved). Tombstoning the three would regenerate `skills/objectstack-ui/references/react-blocks.md` (Tier H) — the claim amendment's reason to keep them is confirmed by the generator's `dataProps` source.

**4. ui breakage — the form-view surfaces are closed; the remaining carriers are the `object-form` block's own, by design.** Fixed here: Studio's New View picker (`anchors.ts`), the `view` default schema (`default-schemas.ts`), and `package-schema.ts` (`modal` → `simple`; its only reader `SchemaForm.tsx:1561` branches on `formType === 'tabbed'`, so the render is unchanged and `PackageFormDialog` keeps the dialog). `view.form.ts` (the spec-side Studio form for `view`) hardcodes no form-type list. MCP / AI authoring tools, `packages/create-objectstack`, templates and seeds: no form-type vocabulary found. Surfaces that can still emit `split` / `drawer` / `modal` are all the **page block `object-form`'s `formType`**, whose schema is `component.zod.ts:6847` with its own section shape (`objectFormSection`, its own `pane` enum at ≈L6800 — not derived from `FormSectionSchema`, so this PR leaks no narrowing onto it): the page-block inspector `previews/block-config.ts:188–196`, `plugin-form/src/index.tsx:295`, `types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:1017`, the console reader set `FormPage.tsx:259`, `form-preview.ts:20`, and `ui/content/docs/api/schema-reference.md:898`. Those produce a block, never a form **view**, and are #27159's per scope note 6465248799; the dev's report names most of them, I add `block-config.ts` and `schema-reference.md:898` (see ③). The renderer's type-check: `RecordFormPage.tsx` compiles as reasoned above; `ObjectForm.tsx` reads its own `ObjectFormSchema` (`types/src/objectql.ts:1833`), untouched. The showcase views render as `tabbed` / `simple`; `navigation: { mode: 'drawer' }` on the default list is a live value. The dev's ui type-checks (types, plugin-form, app-shell incl. `tsconfig.test.json`, console) exited 0 on `edd4570f5`; the CI `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI` and `Test UI` runs on this head are the record (judgment 7).

**5. Tests — re-pinned, nothing weakened.** ui: `view-create-body.test.ts` keeps the three layouts accepted and adds the refusal at `config.type` plus the enum equality; `formSectionGroupReference-7051.test.tsx` turns the two acceptances into refusals with path and message pinned (`['pane']`, `was removed in @objectstack/spec 18.3.0`; `['invalid_value:type']`); `form-spec.containers.test.tsx` and `FormPage.viewSpec.test.ts` move `pane` out of the "was undeclarable" literals into a `@ts-expect-error` pin. One render assertion was deleted — `expect(screen.queryByText('secondary')).not.toBeInTheDocument()` — which asserted the inertness of a key the spec no longer admits; the tsc pin in the same file is the closer-to-code replacement, so this is a re-pin, not a loss. Spec: `view.test.ts` replaces the three `split`-acceptance tests with refusal pins carrying the tombstone's first sentence (sections, groups, defaulted type) and adds the `split` refusal; `view-form-features-root.test.ts` becomes `it.each(['tabbed','wizard'])` (wider than before); `section-group-reference.test.ts` keeps `columns` beside `group`; `view-union-diagnostics.test.ts` adds the retired-type routing case; `view-metadata-schema.test.ts` swaps `splitSize` for `splitDirection` (same vocabulary question). The new pin (31 tests) covers every refusal: 5 doors × 3 values with code, path, first sentence and migrate sentence; `defineStack` envelope; tsc at the authoring site for a value and for both tombstones; `pane` on 3 layouts × 2 buckets; `splitSize` / `splitResizable` on 3 layouts; the stated-boundary acceptance of the four kept keys; conversion, idempotence, load-path absence, wiring, D3; and a tree-scoped absence walk with an anti-vacuity matcher test and visited/mentioning floors. Its regexes judge only `type:` literals in form-view shape — a stated bound; the `index.mdx:234` comment it could not see is fixed by the last commit.

**6. Declarations.** `.changeset/27155-form-view-type-layout-only.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@object-ui/app-shell: minor`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed (…)`; exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker, an HTML comment reading `adr-0087: registered form-view-presentation-types-removed, ui-form-view-type-layout-only` (the `registered ID[, ID]` shape `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:62` reads); `**BREAKING**` banner; FROM → TO and the one-line fix in the body; the kept keys stated. `@object-ui/plugin-form`, `@object-ui/console` and `@objectstack/lint` are touched only in test / fixture files that no `dist` carries (`packages/lint/tsup.config.ts` entries: `index`, `runtime`, `rule-explanations`; the fixture is imported by two tests only), so they publish nothing and owe no changeset (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3). The `ADR-0087:` disposition is also written into the liveness notes and the view.zod.ts comments. Regenerated and consistent: `authorable-surface/ui.json` (three `[RETIRED]`), `content/docs/references/**` (every six-value `type` Enum row on main becomes three), `liveness/state-counts/view.md`. `api-surface` (export names), `react-blocks.md` and `skills/**` are unchanged by construction — `retired-key.ts` §Registration says a value narrowing is byte-invisible to the ratchets, and the tombstones keep each key in the shape. `sdui.manifest.json` is untouched and owes nothing here: it enumerates the ui registry (the block's own schema), and the dev's out-of-scope finding that its `object-form` inputs carry `splitSize` / `splitResizable` is the block's, #27159's. Docs: `views.mdx` Form Types table and the new paragraph, `layout-dsl.mdx` `pane` mention, `index.mdx` example comment — all three handwritten mentions on main are now gone; `pages.mdx` "split pane" is the reader preference (#26804), not this surface. `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — hotcrm src/sales/views/lead.view.ts` is the exact spelling `pm-dispatch/SKILL.md:313` prescribes for an owed follow-up; `skills/**` teaches no retired form-view value (its only six-value list is the block's `formType` in `react-blocks.md:21`, which survives). `Fixes #27155`, `Refs #27153` (not `Part of`, correct since the drawer keys stay), `Ruling-ref: 6464210455`, and #27159 named in Acceptance notes.

**7. Gates (check-runs on `2c75635e`, final reading 2026-10-28T11:44Z; 61 runs).** Conclusions ARE the verdicts; an in_progress run is recorded as in progress, not as a pass. **28 success:** Build Core, Build UI Deps, Build & E2E UI, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path), Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · consumer gates, Plan Test Core shards, Test Core (8/8), Auto Label, filter. **7 skipped** by path filter or opt-in (UI Published Artifacts, Dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness, Schedule gate). **0 failed.** **26 still in progress at this reading:** Test Core (1/8–7/8), Test UI (1/16–16/16), Lint UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace — these are the ui type-check and the test shards the renderer question in judgment 4 rests on; the dev's local runs of the same surfaces (ui type-checks exit 0; 371 spec-reading ui test files 370 passed / 1 skipped; spec `test` 22234 passed; `test:repo` 1355 passed; 112/112 derived gates exit 0, 0 NOT-MEASURED; full dogfood 348 passed / 3 skipped, 2804 tests, on `cd275780d`) are the dev's measurements, not CI's. This record's contract verdict stands on the code reading above; **the Tier S landing condition "every check green" is not yet met at this reading, and the owning seat re-reads the head's check-runs before landing** — a red in any of the 26 reopens this record.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec`: **minor** — correct. The kind is `narrowed` and the arm `(narrowing)`, which AGENTS.md step 3 prices at least `minor` on a package the diff moves; the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition ride with it; ruling 6464210455 (letter A′) and the #24692 B′ / #26804 precedents fix that a narrowing ships as a minor because this repository has no spec-major window, so ADR-0050's own "spec-major" wording does not bind the level. The prescriptions and `retiredAfter: '18.2.0'` name 18.3.0, the next minor from the current 18.2.0, consistently with #26804. `@object-ui/app-shell`: **minor** — a private package (`privatePackages.version: true`, not in the `fixed` group), moved by the diff with the same `narrowed` kind; the #26804 precedent priced its ui consumers `minor` too. No changeset for `plugin-form`, `console`, `lint` (test-only, nothing published). `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0 per the dev; `Check Changeset` green on this head.
